title: Changelog: add rollback via superseding published entries (preserve audit history)
author: Michael Nguyen
description: Problem: we currently have no safe way to correct a published customer-visible model changelog entry. Editing in-place breaks enterprise audit expectations (immutability/tamper-evidence) and creates ambiguity for Support when a customer asks “what did you publish at the time?”. This PR implements a rollback/correction mechanism by superseding published entries with a new published entry while preserving the original forever. Approach: Introduce a first-class “supersedes” relationship on changelog entries. A rollback creates a new entry (new entry_id, new event_id, new published_at) that references the prior entry as superseded, and marks the prior entry as superseded_by=<new>. We do not delete or mutate the original entry body post-publication. API changes: Add POST /v1/model-changelog/entries/{entry_id}:supersede (internal/authz) to create a corrected entry, and add query params include_superseded=true and resolve=latest|all to the read endpoints used by Console and docs publishing. Default behavior remains resolve=latest (i.e., customers see the corrected entry by default), but the full history is retrievable for audit/support via include_superseded=true (subject to RBAC). Audit logging: Emit a new audit event type changelog.entry.superseded capturing actor, reason, superseded_entry_id, new_entry_id, and the hash of both payloads. This aligns with Security/Compliance requirements for immutable retention and “who changed what, when” without requiring data deletion. Notes: This is intentionally not a generic edit API for published entries; only “supersede” is supported once status=published. Backfill/migration sets superseded_by null for existing entries. Follow-ups: console UI will surface “This entry supersedes…” banner and allow viewing prior text behind an internal-only toggle; docs site will show only the latest entry (history available in the JSON feed when include_superseded=true).
commits: changelog: add supersede relationship + DB migration
api: implement supersede endpoint + RBAC checks
read endpoints: add resolve/include_superseded params + tests
docs/publish: ensure generator picks latest entry for a version
tests: integration coverage for supersede chain + pagination
conversation: Jada Williams (workflow): Can we confirm state machine constraints? I don’t want an operator to “rollback” a draft and accidentally publish something. Author (Michael): Good call—added a guard: only status=published entries can be superseded; drafts/in_review will 400 with a clear error. Connor O’Brien (release eng): What’s the intended operator workflow during a hotfix? We need a reason captured for enterprise and a way to link to the correction in release comms. Author: Endpoint requires reason (string, min len 10) and we include it in the audit event. Also the response returns a canonical changelog_url for the new entry to use in comms. Jordan Lee (RBAC): Who can call the supersede endpoint? Should match publish permissions, not edit permissions. Author: Implemented authz: requires role release_notes.publisher OR model_registry.admin; basic metadata editors cannot supersede. Added unit tests for denial paths. Marcus Lin (security): Please ensure we don’t allow unbounded supersede chains that could be abused (spam). Also do we hash the payload pre/post? Author: Added max chain depth of 5 (configurable) and a rate limit per actor. Audit event includes sha256 of canonical JSON for both entries (precomputed server-side). Naomi Feldman (compliance): We need language that the original remains immutable and retrievable for audit. Is the read endpoint gated? Author: include_superseded=true is gated behind internal tiers/roles; customer-facing docs/feeds default resolve=latest and do not expose superseded text unless explicitly enabled for the enterprise feed contract (future). Chloe Martin (console backend): Pagination semantics with resolve=all look tricky; do we order by published_at or event_id? Author: Ordered by published_at desc then entry_id for stability; superseded entries appear immediately after their latest replacement when resolve=all (server-side grouping). Added deterministic ordering tests. Final review: Connor approved after verifying hotfix workflow. Marcus approved after confirming hashes + immutability. Jada approved after state checks landed. Naomi approved after audit wording in API docs was updated.
merge_outcome: Merged to main; will ship behind feature flag changelog_supersede_enabled and enabled in staging by default.
